body:
`person:group-gensol-jaggi` · flag: **severe** · confidence: verified · tickers: GENSOL

Flag: SEVERE. Gensol Engineering (solar EPC; EV leasing to sister company BluSmart, both promoted by the Jaggi brothers) was a 2022-24 smallcap multibagger. SEBI's interim order (15-Apr-2025) found prima facie that of ~Rs 978 cr borrowed from IREDA and PFC to buy 6,400 EVs for BluSmart, only ~4,704 were bought (~Rs 568 cr); funds were round-tripped via the vehicle supplier and related entities to promoters' uses (incl. a luxury DLF Camellias apartment and personal spending); promoters treated the listed company 'like a personal piggy bank'; letters purportedly from lenders submitted to rating agencies (CARE, ICRA) were allegedly forged; SEBI barred the Jaggis from the market and from director roles and halted a stock split. SEBI confirmed the interim directions (Jul-2025); the Jaggis resigned from the board. IREDA's petition admitted Gensol into insolvency (Jun-2025, ~Rs 510 cr default); NCLT Ahmedabad admitted BluSmart (Jul-2025). CBI registered an FIR (31-Jul-2025) over alleged misappropriation of IREDA loans (~Rs 672 cr cited); ED searches/forex probe; MCA examination. Criminal cases are pending. Early signals visible in 2024: rating-agency downgrades to default after 'forged' no-default letters were questioned, related-party leasing to the sponsor's unlisted startup, preferential allotments and a stock split proposal amid soaring price, and rapid debt growth versus cash flow.

- **regulator findings:** SEBI interim Apr-2025, confirmed Jul-2025 (fund diversion)

body:
1. **Conservative ranges, then raises.** Every company except A. O. Smith beat or raised its 2025–26 guidance. A beat is the base case for an explicit US range on a company-level number. **A 100% delivery record here mostly measures how conservative the guide is.** That is the main difference from India, where the same metric mostly measured execution.
2. **Wide bands make "delivered" cheap.** Simpson's 2-point operating-margin band and Lincoln's "mid single digit" words are hard to miss. Specificity weights (range 2, vague 1) only partly correct for this.
3. **Tariffs, steel and price/cost in 2025–26** were named on every call. Price actions held margins (Watts price ~8% in Q1-26; Simpson's 2025 price actions ~$130 mn annualised vs $100 mn; Lincoln "neutral price-cost posture"). A. O. Smith is the exception: steel +15–20% and weak residential volume compressed its North America margin.
4. **Capex and plant timing are the weak point, as in India.** Simpson 2025 capex 0.6% over its range and Gallatin ramp-up late; A. O. Smith 2025 capex 6% under; Lincoln 2026 capex raised from $110–130 mn to $140–150 mn (pending). The sample is small (n=4 scored), but the direction matches T&D and auto components.
5. **Adjusted vs GAAP.** Watts, A. O. Smith and Lincoln guide *adjusted* figures (excluding restructuring and acquisition costs). Simpson guides GAAP (including property-sale gains). The calls resolve each on the basis the company guided: adjusted through an 8-K scan (assisted), GAAP through XBRL (structured).

- **v1 · 2026-11-20.** First version, from the Vishal Mega Mart practice run (retailer).
- **v1.1 · 2026-11-21.** From the Cummins India practice run (manufacturer, 51% MNC subsidiary):
  - Added the unit-by-business-type table.
  - L4 now ranks cost lines by weight before going deep.
  - L5 time share is 15% for MNC subsidiaries, with a parent-take table and the AGM-notice RPT annex as a source.
  - L2 additions: customer concentration, other-income decomposition and the screener exceptional-item trap.
  - New techniques #13–18: BRSR intensity → units; commodity pass-through lag; transfer-pricing bounds; regulatory-transition template; own vs group capacity; concentration → channel map. Demand-side physics check added under #12.
  - Added manufacturer data sources and B2B scuttlebutt rules.
  - Two new deliverables, four new traps and a tool note.
- **v1.2 · 2026-11-21.** From the Five Below practice run (US specialty retailer, first US filer):
  - Rewrote the US data-source table by layer, with tools.
  - Added the US 10-K item/note reading list (with a year-over-year text diff), the SBC handling rule, and Form 4 / 13F / 13G reading rules.
  - Added a "US widely held company" row to the unit table (management as the related party).
  - New techniques #19 (store model vs capex guidance), #20 (rent per new lease from the lease note), #21 (tariff cost from refunds and duty math), #22 (guidance implied-remainder and split promise tracking) and #23 (US payroll estimate).
  - One new deliverable line and six new traps/tool notes.
- **v1.3 · 2026-11-22.** From the Federal Bank end-to-end dry run (stages 2→6; first lender):
  - Added the **S2 checklist** step before L1 (every disqualifier-v2 rule with a dated source), so the card is never "incomplete".
  - Added **L8 valuation and decision** (worksheet + card + paper calls) per `research_notes/Templates/valuation_and_decision.md` §5, with the extra inputs it needs (two-source close, 10 FY-end P/Es or P/Bs, peers, ADV, dilution).
  - Added the **Bank / NBFC adaptation** section: S2 in bank form, lender units (branch, segment, liability pool, balance-sheet cost lines), physical cost drivers (IBA scale, DICGC, CRR, PSL shortfall), rate/funding mechanics, asset-quality walk, valuation in bank mode, signal caveats, NBFC differences to test next.
  - Replaced the one-line "Lender" row in the unit table.
  - Three deliverable lines; seven traps/tool notes.
  - Tools changed with it: `tools/valuation/bank.py` (+ `worksheet.py` dispatch), `tools/decision/decision_card.py` (bank stage-5 text), `tools/promise_tracker/pipeline/` (bank measures, cover-letter handling, `--local`, quarter detection, range-parse and chain fixes, `bank_kpis.py`), `tools/nse_fetch.py integrated`.
- **v1.4 · 2026-11-23.** From the first three live dives (SUNFLAG, US-KEX, AUTOAXLES; lessons L33–L38):
  - Added a one-page **deep-dive checklist** at the top (every layer and its mandatory output).
  - Added **S0 selection and scoreability** for live dives: rules written first, seeded draw, logged skips, entity must exist through the call horizon (`decision:live-dd-selection-rules`).
  - Added **holding-company / non-operating stakes** (separate valuation, stub analysis, discount explained by verified causes before calling mispricing; L33).
  - Added **cyclicals**: normalised (10-yr) EPS and the peak-cycle test whenever the stock screens cheap; full-cycle ROIIC windows (L38; valuation README v1.3 calibration note).
  - L5: follow fees/royalties to the parent; read shareholder vote results; materials-ratio check when a related-party channel changes (L16, L38).
  - Stage 3 for no-concall companies: annual-report mode asset × year table and disclosure flags (L37; promise-tracker pipeline v1.4).
  - L8: worksheet v1.3 inputs (cash tax, ROIIC realism, exit-multiple bet table) and card v1.2 (India survival cap, tail anchoring to base rates; L34–L36).
  - Six deliverable lines; five traps/tool notes. No earlier text removed.
